topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Hallmarks and Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: The lecture opens with framing on the learning outcomes, previous lectures, and the general framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Signaling Pathways Driving Proliferation and Survival
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in receptor tyrosine kinase and Wnt/beta-catenin cascades enable self-sufficient growth signaling and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation Block in Neoplasia
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how failure of cells to execute terminal differentiation promotes malignancy in leukemias and colorectal tissue.

topics.label: Resistance to Apoptosis via the p53 Pathway
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how cancer cells avoid programmed cell death through mutations in p53 and the dysregulation of pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins.

topics.label: Replicative Immortality, Telomeres, and Senescence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the mechanisms of telomere shortening, telomerase reactivation, and cellular senescence bypass in cancer cells.

topics.label: Metabolic Reprogramming and the Warburg Effect
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells rewire their metabolic pathways to support rapid biosynthetic demand and epigenetic changes.

topics.label: Induction of Tumor Angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the physiological necessity and regulatory balance governing new blood vessel formation to sustain tumor growth.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Dynamics of Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the multistep metastatic cascade, circulation dynamics, the seed-and-soil hypothesis, and the genomic features of metastases.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Practical Framing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecture concludes with summary reflections on the integration of cancer hallmarks and housekeeping information for upcoming sessions.
